Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `XmlStreamWriterTest_testNoXmlHeader.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/commons-io/manual/testcases/XmlStreamWriterTest/XmlStreamWriterTest_testNoXmlHeader.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I have both files. The original test only exercises `testNoXmlHeader`, which calls `checkXmlContent` directly — but the file carries a lot of dead code (four `TEXT_*` constants, `checkXmlWriter` overloads, `createXmlContent`, and an unused `DefaultLocale` import) that has nothing to do with this test. I'll keep the exercised behavior identical while removing the noise and clarifying the one helper that actually runs.Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). I removed the dead code (unused `TEXT_*` constants, `checkXmlWriter`/`createXmlContent` helpers, and the unused `DefaultLocale` import), renamed the one exercised helper to `assertWrittenEncoding`, and added doc comments — all while keeping the same call (`assertWrittenEncoding("<text>...</text>", "UTF-8", null)`) and assertions, so runtime behavior is unchanged.
